new.title: See van de Velde's interior at the Osthaus Museum
new.desc: The Karl Ernst Osthaus Museum in Hagen was built in 1902 as the original Museum Folkwang, with an interior by Henry van de Velde. Today it holds main collections of Christian Rohlfs and Emil Schumacher, plus environmental art by Herman de Vries.
new.tip: Check osthausmuseum.de for hours and combine it with the nearby Emil Schumacher Museum.

new.title: Step into Van de Velde's Villa Hohenhof in Hagen
new.desc: Villa Hohenhof was built 1906-08 by Henry van de Velde for the patron Karl Ernst Osthaus, who also had him design the furniture, lamps and crockery. It is the museum of the Hagen Impulse, an early modern art and architecture movement.
new.tip: Open weekends 11:00-18:00 (about EUR 3); public tours run in spring, with registration via the VHS.

new.title: Visit the moated castle and archaeology museum at Werdringen
new.desc: Wasserschloss Werdringen in Hagen-Vorhalle houses the Archaeology Museum Hagen, opened in 2004, covering about 450 million years of regional history. A life-size mammoth replica greets visitors and finds from the Balver Höhle are displayed.
new.tip: A small cafe runs during museum hours; combine it with a walk on the Harkortsee shore.

new.title: Peer at the Köpchenwerk pumped-storage hall in Herdecke
new.desc: Built 1927-30 by RWE and named after planner Arthur Köpchen, this was one of Germany's first big pumped-storage plants (132 MW) and closed in 1994. It is a listed monument on the Route der Industriekultur beside the Hengsteysee.
new.tip: The turbine hall is mostly closed but visible from the lakeside path; guided tours are announced by industriedenkmal-stiftung.de.

new.title: Spot the Colani-Ei UFO on a Lünen pit headframe
new.desc: The Colani-Ei (Lüntec Tower) is the former headframe of Zeche Minister Achenbach in Brambauer, remodelled to a sketch by Luigi Colani and finished in May 1995. The 20 m wide egg sits atop the tower with a lounge at 35 m.
new.tip: Best seen from outside; the lounge is mainly for events and bookings.
new.q: Colani-Ei, Zeche Minister Achenbach, Brambauer, Lünen

new.title: Visit the Bahnhof Langendreer culture station
new.desc: The former Prussian transfer station at Langendreer was built in 1908 as one of the largest in Germany and is now a cultural centre with a cafe. It sits on the Route der Industriekultur.
new.tip: Check the programme for concerts, readings and cinema.

new.title: Walk the shore of the Harkortsee
new.desc: The Harkortsee on the Ruhr is 3.2 km long and 1.37 sq km, with water sports, boat rental, minigolf and bouldering. A passenger boat links Wetter and Herdecke from April to October.
new.tip: Start at the Wetter landing and watch the Ruhr viaduct at the Hagen end.

new.title: Cruise the Ruhr on the MS Schwalbe II from Witten
new.desc: The MS Schwalbe II is run by Stadtwerke Witten on the Kemnader See and Ruhr, season April to October. Summer evening Beats & Cruise trips depart from the Freizeitbad Heveney landing from mid-May to early September 2026.
new.tip: Book via schwalbe.stadtwerke-witten.de or 02302 9173-450.

new.title: Stroll the Kurpark and Gradierwerk in Bad Hamm
new.desc: The Kurpark in Bad Hamm was laid out in 1883-84 after a brine spring was found, with ponds, old trees and an elephant-shaped flower bed. The brine graduation tower is about 42 m long.
new.tip: Free to enter; the Maximare thermal baths are nearby.

new.title: Soak at the Maximare thermal baths in Hamm
new.desc: Maximare Erlebnistherme opened in November 2003 in Bad Hamm and combines water slides, brine pools and a sauna area.
new.tip: Ask for current prices and hours at the baths; busiest on rainy weekends.

new.title: Swim at the Cappenberger See lido in Lünen
new.desc: The Freibad at the Cappenberger See in northern Lünen has a 50 m sports pool and is run by the Bädergesellschaft Lünen. The lake nearby offers sailing and boat rental.
new.tip: Typically open May to September, adult day ticket around EUR 5.40; confirm on baeder-luenen.de.
new.q: Freibad Cappenberger See, Borker Straße 56, Lünen

new.title: Browse the Hörder Neumarkt weekly market
new.desc: The Hörder Neumarkt market in Dortmund-Hörde takes place on Thursdays from 7:00 to 13:00. Dortmund markets generally run 7:00-13:00.
new.tip: Combine with a walk up to the Phoenix See.

new.title: Shop the Hohenlimburg weekly market in Hagen
new.desc: The Wochenmarkt Hohenlimburg takes place on Gaußstraße on Fridays 7:00-13:00, with regional produce stalls.
new.tip: Pair it with a visit to Schloss Hohenlimburg.

new.title: Catch an event at the Elbershallen in Hagen
new.desc: The Elbershallen is a leisure and culture factory in a former industrial building on Dödterstraße in Hagen, hosting concerts, parties and markets.
new.tip: Check the programme before you go.

new.title: Wander the old town and Bachviertel of Herdecke
new.desc: Herdecke's old town above the Ruhr has a pedestrian zone, small shops and cafes around the Bachviertel.
new.tip: Walk down to the Ruhr bridge for the Harkortsee boat.

new.title: Follow the beer history tour in Dortmund-Hörde
new.desc: A guided walk through Hörde tells how the district went from steel workers' after-work beer to craft beer, including tastings.
new.tip: Book through the operator in advance.

new.title: Have cake at Goldberg's Törtchen in Hagen
new.desc: Goldberg's Törtchen at Goldbergstraße 4 serves cakes, tarts and waffles with coffee specialties, plus small lunches, with vegan choices.
new.tip: Takeaway available; oat and almond milk on offer.

new.title: Try creative cakes at raum cafe in Witten
new.desc: raum cafe in Witten's Wiesenviertel is a coffeehouse known for creative cakes and specialty coffee.
new.tip: Same address as Knut's at Wiesenstraße 25.

new.title: Eat and hear live music at Knut's in Witten
new.desc: Knut's is a restaurant and bar in Witten's Wiesenstraße with an unconventional menu and live music.
new.tip: Check the events page for concert nights.

new.title: Eat organic at liebbar in Herdecke
new.desc: liebbar is a cafe, restaurant and bar at Alte Stiftsstraße 4a with organic, vegan and regional dishes.
new.tip: Good stop after the old town walk.

new.title: Have coffee at Das Wunderland in Hamm
new.desc: Das Wunderland at Martin-Luther-Straße 35 is a salon theatre and art cafe in Hamm.
new.tip: Check opening and show dates.

new.title: Sip coffee at Baristoteles in Bochum
new.desc: Baristoteles at Schlossstraße 1A is a cafe that doubles as an event space and coffee museum.
new.tip: Try a pour-over.

new.title: Eat regional at Ruhrfeuer by the Jahrhunderthalle
new.desc: Ruhrfeuer is a regional bistro in the Pumpenhaus next to the Jahrhunderthalle, with vegan and vegetarian options.
new.tip: Pair with a stroll in the Westpark.

new.title: Take a long coffee break at Fräulein Coffea in Bochum
new.desc: Fräulein Coffea at Oskar-Hoffmann-Straße 34 is a cake-focused cafe with a vintage interior.
new.tip: Go for the cakes.

new.title: Eat vegan brunch at Blondies in Bochum
new.desc: Blondies on Hattinger Straße 80 is a cafe, restaurant and bar with vegan, vegetarian and organic food.
new.tip: Popular at weekends.

new.title: Order brunch at omarosa in Dortmund
new.desc: omarosa is a brunch cafe on Chemnitzer Straße with its own pastry shop.
new.tip: Arrive early at weekends.

new.title: Sit in the courtyard at Hofcafe Unionsviertel
new.desc: Hofcafe Unionsviertel at Huckarder Straße 10-12 is a courtyard cafe near Dortmund's centre.
new.tip: Best in summer.

new.title: Grab cake and coffee at Hi Kalle in Bochum
new.desc: Hi Kalle at Am Kortländer 2 is a small cafe with snacks, cakes and coffee.
new.tip: Close to the Bermuda3Eck.
